answer: Practically, the chain should bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because violet only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. In practice comet is enforced by the ledger itself: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any signal approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
